briefing.opening: Good morning/afternoon, everyone. I will now begin the climate briefing for September 22, 2026.

sections.title: 🔴 The Severity and Spread of the Climate Crisis
sections.content: News reported today warns that the climate crisis is intensifying globally. Flash floods in the Nepal-Tibet region and the deepening Himalayan flood disasters clearly demonstrate the increased risk of catastrophe exacerbated by climate change [8, 153, 154], while Spain is battling climate change with summer wildfires and heatwaves [159]. In California, a helicopter crash during wildfire suppression resulted in casualties, highlighting the severity of climate-related disasters [164]. With the realization of a 'Super El Niño,' countries have declared states of emergency, and calls for strengthened climate action have successively emerged at the UN General Assembly [21], and the World Meteorological Organization (WMO) has reported a decrease in the Earth's freshwater reserves, warning of a breakdown in the water cycle [14, 150]. This global crisis, coupled with analyses indicating that climate change is affecting public health and health security domestically [2], suggests an urgent need for action.

sections.title: 🌍 International Community's Response to and Awareness of Climate Change
sections.content: Global leaders gathered at the UN, addressing climate change as a major agenda item alongside war and artificial intelligence [134, 148, 156, 158]. Japanese Prime Minister Takaichi also emphasized the issue of climate change at the UN, stressing the need for a concerted international response [11], and analyses suggest that climate change and energy transition are now emerging as core national security issues [136]. Meanwhile, the acceptance of human-caused climate change among the U.S. population remains stable [142], and efforts are being made to link climate action with health security through a One Health approach [139]. However, an inequitable outlook has been raised, suggesting that even if global greenhouse gas emissions are reduced to net-zero, the poorest populations, especially those in tropical regions, will be the last to experience the benefits of climate crisis mitigation [161], leaving the issue of equity in international cooperation as a challenge to be addressed.

sections.title: 🇰🇷 Domestic Climate Action and Carbon Neutrality Efforts
sections.content: Various local governments and organizations across the country have shown active movements towards practicing carbon neutrality and responding to climate change. Chungju City aims to raise awareness of climate change and carbon neutrality through a special lecture by invited author Lee Jeong-mo [1, 16, 18, 22], while Guri City and Seogwipo Elementary School successfully conducted climate change science camps and field experiences for families and students [4, 6, 9, 10, 15, 20]. Seongdong-gu is creating 'Seongdong's Seasons,' a garden resilient to climate change [5, 17, 24], and Geumcheon-gu plans to actively discover climate response projects by introducing a greenhouse gas reduction awareness budget system [23, 26]. Furthermore, Suwon citizens achieved an annual per capita carbon reduction effect of 1.1 tons through two weeks of carbon neutrality practices [31], and Seoul youth practiced carbon neutrality by reducing waste at universities and festivals, encouraging citizen participation [27, 36, 44].

sections.title: 🌱 Accelerating Renewable Energy Transition and Innovation
sections.content: Various efforts and innovations to accelerate the renewable energy transition have continued. Jeju Island is pursuing a plan to invest 323.2 billion KRW to transform aging industrial complexes into innovation hubs for renewable energy and clean bio-industries [70, 74, 81, 82, 103, 107, 108, 118, 120, 121], and in Yeongam, the construction of a 2GW renewable energy complex has officially begun [96]. KEPCO E&C is strengthening its development and investment in renewable energy projects, including offshore wind and solar power, through cooperation with Truston Asset Management [73, 76, 78, 83, 92, 93, 125, 129], and Solaroncare is seeking technological innovation by hosting renewable energy generation prediction competitions with POSTECH, KAIST, and others [71, 95, 104, 109, 112, 124]. Notably, renewable energy siting regulations have been significantly improved, such as the removal of the '1km barrier' applied to solar power generation facilities, which is expected to positively impact the expansion of their deployment [84]. These efforts are leading to the growth of related industries, with companies like Taihan Electric Wire experiencing their biggest boom since their founding due to AI and renewable energy special demand [86].

sections.title: ⚠️ Challenges and Policy Tasks of the Renewable Energy Transition
sections.content: Despite the importance of the renewable energy transition, many challenges and policy tasks remain. The International Renewable Energy Agency (IRENA) warned that the current pace of renewable energy deployment is too slow, requiring a doubling of annual deployment to meet 2030 targets [97], and criticism has been raised that South Korea's renewable energy transition is relatively slow [99]. The Korean Nuclear Society argued for public discourse that considers not only nuclear power costs but also renewable energy costs [114], and concerns about a 'predetermined conclusion' style of discussion have been raised regarding the government's public discourse on nuclear power utilization, premised on expanding electricity demand [131], suggesting a need for in-depth discussion on the direction of energy policy. Furthermore, while solar power and heat pumps are gaining attention in the climate industry, the hydrogen industry has been observed to falter due to policy uncertainties [49]. With successive controversies surrounding recruitment and executive appointments at the Sinan New & Renewable Energy Foundation [116], institutional improvements are also needed to ensure the transparency and healthy growth of renewable energy projects.

briefing.closing: Today's briefing highlighted the severe reality of the climate crisis, along with various response efforts underway both domestically and internationally, and the challenges of the renewable energy transition. It is time for comprehensive efforts towards a sustainable future to be further accelerated. This concludes today's climate briefing.
